_comment: FAST Problematic Windows Update Database
Read by ProblematicKbs.cs and rendered as System Score check 47 (Windows Updates, 5 pts).
An entry fires only when its KB is installed AND its resolvedBy fix is not.
FIELDS THE CODE READS - change these and you change what users are told:
id             - the KB exactly as Get-HotFix reports it, e.g. KB5063060. Matched
case-insensitively. A KB superseded by a later cumulative update stops
appearing in Get-HotFix at all, so an entry can go quiet on its own.
issue          - what the user LOSES, in their words. Sentence fragment, no trailing
period. Rendered as '<ids> - <issue>. <recommendation>'.
recommendation - what to do about it, and the ONLY place that action lives. The score
line no longer appends 'uninstall' to everything. Do not reach for
uninstall by reflex: dropping a cumulative update costs the user every
security fix riding in it, so it is right only when the regression is
severe and no fix has shipped. Omit the field and the entry states the
issue without prescribing anything.
resolvedBy     - OPTIONAL. The KB that repairs the issue. When the user has both, this
entry says nothing, because Microsoft already fixed it and there is no
action left. Set it the moment a fix ships. It is the field that stops a
stale entry telling people to uninstall a problem they no longer have.
FIELDS THE CODE DOES NOT READ - provenance for whoever reviews the next change:
lastUpdated    - date the entries below last CHANGED. The watch routine opens a PR only
when something actually moves, so this is not the date of the last
review - the routine's own run history is where that lives.
source         - the page the claim came from. Required on every NEW entry: an entry
nobody can re-check is an entry nobody can safely retire later.
KB5063060 was deleted on 2026-09-24: its own KB page shows it FIXED the
Easy Anti-Cheat restarts from KB5060842. KB5066835 ('frame rates drop on
NVIDIA GPUs') was deleted on 2026-10-20: it predated this field, rested
only on a Guru3D thread, and Windows release health never documented a
gaming fault for it (re-checked 2026-09-10 and 2026-10-20).
AN EMPTY kbs LIST IS VALID: no update is flagged and check 47 passes. Only a file that
fails to load skips the check.
WHEN TO DELETE AN ENTRY INSTEAD OF RESOLVING IT
resolvedBy means 'the update was at fault and a later update fixed it'. If the update
turns out NOT to be the cause, delete the entry outright - there is no user-facing value
in remembering a false alarm, and leaving it costs the user 5 points for nothing. The
August 2026 KB5121003 game-crash reports are the worked example: Microsoft traced the
cause to a third-party RGB driver (inpoutx64.sys), not the update, so KB5121003 must
never appear in this file no matter how the tech press headlined it.
There is deliberately no severity field. Check 47 is binary, 5 points or 0, so a severity
would have looked like it graded the outcome while changing nothing - the same dead-field
trap that recommendation was in until 2026-09-05.
